chunks: Layth al-Murādī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who has a nosebleed from the sun’s zenith until the night passes. He said:
"He gestures with his head for each salat (prayer)."

key_terms.إِيمَاءً: a gesturing motion used in place of normal prayer movements
key_terms.زَوَالَ: the sun’s decline from the meridian; noon-time onset

ai.seo_question: What should a person do for salat (prayer) if he has continuous nosebleeding from noon until night?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for someone afflicted with continuous nosebleeding over the period of multiple prayers. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام instructs that such a person should perform the prayer by gesturing with the head for each salat (prayer), indicating accommodation in worship during incapacity.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1055 - Layth al-Muradi asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) about a man who suffers from continuous nosebleeds from the time of the sun's zenith until nightfall.
Imam (as) replied: "He should gesture with his head for each prayer."
